memo.verdict: PROGRESS to Early-Stage Assessment, medium conviction, direction NEUTRAL. The memo explicitly overrules the risks-family report, whose stage-progression section recommends a hold-and-watch, watch-list stance (a park verdict). Progression is conditional and reversible on one dated test: the Q1 FY2026/27 interim report on 28 August 2026. Park immediately if that print shows gross margin below 36.0% together with organic growth below 4%, which is the earnings-review report's own falsification test and would mean the 1 June 2026 global price increase failed. Three further park triggers: restructuring charges above SEK 30m in H1 FY2026/27; adjusted operating margin below 9%; a second regional market joining the Nordics in negative organic growth. Sequencing instruction is explicit: run the Early-Stage Assessment memo AFTER the 28 August 2026 print, not before, so price-realisation evidence is in hand. First ESA task is the entry point (Element E3), because the multiple, not the change forces, is the unresolved variable.
case: - The Triaging stage test is whether the case has large amounts of positive change forces. It does, and that is the whole basis of the progression recommendation.

- External change is legislated, not discretionary. The revised Energy Performance of Buildings Directive cuts the mandatory building-automation and control threshold from 290kW to 70kW by 2027, requires 25% of the worst-performing building stock renovated, and requires all new buildings to be zero-emission by 2030. Fluorinated-gas rules ban new units above 150 global-warming potential from January 2027 and mandate an 80% cut in hydrofluorocarbons by 2030. Deep renovation rates must accelerate from 0.2% to 3.0% of stock annually. Buildings consume about 40% of European final energy and generate 36% of emissions.

- The pull-through is already visible: equipment upgrade and retrofit revenue grew 33% year on year; taxonomy-aligned turnover rose to 28% from 27%, with 42% taxonomy-eligible; delivered heat-recovery units cut property energy demand by an estimated 2.0 terawatt-hours in FY25/26.
counter_case: - The risks-family report recommends PARK and the memo says so explicitly. Its stage-progression section states the investment should sit on a watch-list until Nordic residential starts recover and Menerga's Slovenian margins are fully verified, and its progression verdict is a hold-and-watch stance because the potential 25% internal rate of return is highly sensitive to volatile European building renovation rates. It assesses aggregated failure probability as medium-high.

- Its winning hypothesis is the FALSE FRIEND profile, which its Analysis of Competing Hypotheses matrix scores with zero hard inconsistencies against current operational data: strong Western European organic sales growth masking under-utilised global factories and persistent cash-draining restructurings. The memo states what that finding actually rests on (operating leverage, cash conversion and a SEK 35.8m adjusted-to-reported gap), routes all three to Element E1 Required Attribute 2 (Robust base) where they are stated in full, declines to let them drive the false-friend grade, and explicitly refuses to treat the matrix as independent corroboration because the three-profile framework is Richard's own.
triggers: - The dated catalyst: Q1 FY2026/27 interim report, 28 August 2026. Park if gross margin falls below 36.0% together with organic growth below 4%. This is the earnings-review report's own falsification test and would mean the 1 June 2026 global price increase failed.
- Second park trigger: restructuring charges above SEK 30m in H1 FY2026/27, the risks report's clean-stabilisation test.
- Third park trigger: adjusted operating margin below 9%, the peer-average line at which the risks report requires a full pre-mortem re-run.
- Fourth park trigger: a second regional market joining the Nordics in negative organic growth, since geographic diversification is the current defence.
- What would raise conviction to high: a bottom-quartile multiple appearing alongside confirmed price realisation, which would convert the partial trough-on-trough fit into a full one.
- What would NOT change the answer: another quarter of strong Eastern European or North American growth alone, because the case turns on Western Europe and on price.
